conviction_note: Nine small findings that roughly offset, net +0.7 by finding size. Positives: a low EPS bar, pricing discipline, H2 free cash flow and capex arithmetic, and depressed sector positioning. Negatives: a very tough postpaid net-add comp and the activation-fee ARPU drag. The scaled number is abs_move 5.0 x (2x0.53-1) = +0.30, because nothing found is a decisive company-level number the market lacks; the stock has traded on FCF/guidance and subscriber lines (Q1'26 EPS miss yet +11% intraday on an FCF raise; Q2'26 small beat yet -4.1%), not on EPS.
bar: Q3 2026 consensus per Yahoo Finance Canada (RCI-B.TO): adj EPS C$1.24 (14 analysts, range 1.12-1.35, year-ago 1.37), revenue C$5.40B (13 analysts, range 5.31-5.53, year-ago 5.35B) https://ca.finance.yahoo.com/quote/RCI-B.TO/analysis/ . Disputed: Chartmill snippet C$1.28 / C$5.542B (https://www.chartmill.com/stock/quote/RCI/estimates, 403, snippet only); MarketBeat US$0.85 / US$3.79B (~C$1.18 at the Q2 conversion) https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-10-23-rogers-communications-inc-stock/ . EPS sources broadly agree around C$1.18-1.28; revenue sources disagree, so EPS-based findings are capped small. No company quarterly guide; FY2026 guide is service revenue +3-5%, adj EBITDA +1-3%, capex C$2.5-2.7B, FCF C$4.1-4.3B (Q2 2026 deck, https://about.rogers.com/wp-content/uploads/RCI-Q2-2026.pdf).
positioning_check: NYSE RCI short interest 14,192,170 shares at the 2026-09-30 settlement (2.6% of shares), 9.89 days to cover on NYSE-only volume (overstates DTC because most volume trades on the TSX). Down from 18,074,453 on 2026-08-31; model estimate for 10-15 is ~14.75M (https://equibles.com/stocks/rci/shortinterest, fetched 2026-10-22). Not a crowded short. No usable option chain: the ATM spread is 127% of mid, skew null, and put/call OI 3.08 on only 469 contracts, so there is no directional statement. Tape: spot US$32.93, 19.6% below the 52-week high, 10.6% above the 52-week low, +3.1% over 5 days, +2.1% over 20 days. The Globe (2026-10-18) puts Rogers -13% YTD and the TSX telecom index -16% YTD versus the TSX +11%, on bond yields, SpaceX spectrum fears and price competition.

findings.finding: Consensus adj EPS of C$1.24 (14 analysts) implies -9.5% YoY against Q3'25's C$1.37. Rogers' own H1'26 adj diluted EPS rose +1% (C$2.17 vs 2.14) and Q2 adj net income to shareholders rose +3%. Last year's Q3 estimate was also C$1.24 and the actual was 1.37 (+10.4%), and Rogers has beaten EPS in 3 of the last 4 quarters.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: EPS does not drive this stock. Q1'26 adj EPS C$1.01 vs 1.02 estimate (a miss), yet the shares rose >11% intraday on the FCF/capex guide (rbr.com 2026-04-22). Q2'26 C$1.15 vs 1.13 (a beat) and the shares fell 4.1% (baseline 2026-07-22 bmo). Q4'25 +7.6% beat with a +5% intraday move (itiger).
findings.why_not_priced: The estimate trend is flat (1.24 now, 1.26 30-60 days ago), so no one has revised toward the H1 run-rate. If the market expected a beat, revisions would have drifted up into the print, as they did not. But the bar is disputed (C$1.18-1.28 across sources) and EPS is not the line this stock trades on.
findings.independence: Q2 2026 press release (https://about.rogers.com/wp-content/uploads/Rogers-Q2-2026-Press-Release.pdf) gives H1 adj EPS +1%. Q3'25 actual C$1.37 is from https://finviz.com/news/201756/rogers-communications-reports-third-quarter-2025-results . Shares the cost-program driver with the cost-savings finding below.

findings.finding: Postpaid phone net adds face a very hard comp. Q3'25 was 62,000 postpaid and 111,000 total. Q2'26 was 22,000 postpaid (-34% YoY) and 40,000 total. At the CIBC conference (Quartr summary dated 2026-10-01), management said sector volumes are down on fewer international students and churn is roughly flat with minor increases tied to its own price actions. Q3'26 postpaid adds of roughly 20-35k (-45% to -65% YoY) look likely.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2'26 net adds down 34% YoY plus the MLSE charge: shares -4.1% on the day (baseline 2026-07-22 bmo; RTTNews 'shares down in pre-market' https://www.rttnews.com/3669326/rogers-communications-turns-to-loss-in-q2-reaffirms-fy26-outlook-shares-down-in-pre-market.aspx?type=cn).
findings.why_not_priced: The weak volume trend is public, and analysts (JPMorgan, TD in April) have cut net-add numbers, so much of it is expected. What may be unpriced is the size of the YoY drop against the 62k Q3'25 comp, plus management's own admission of churn creep from price actions. If fully priced, the stock would not have bounced 3% in the last five days.
findings.independence: Q3'25 comp: https://finviz.com/news/201756/rogers-communications-reports-third-quarter-2025-results . Q2'26 trend: https://about.rogers.com/wp-content/uploads/Rogers-Q2-2026-Press-Release.pdf . Macro proxy: Canada lost 68,300 jobs in September (https://www.theglobeandmail.com/investing/markets/inside-the-market/market-news/article-stock-futures-gain-as-oil-slips-telecoms-pressured-by-spacex-spectrum/).

findings.finding: Signs of wireless pricing discipline. Desjardins (2026-09-14 upgrade to Buy) and management at CIBC both say back-to-school discounting was quiet or lighter. In early October, Bell, then Rogers and Telus, raised entry plans by $5 a month, so all three now start at $70/60GB. Bell also put a $6/month increase on existing customers' October bills. This gives management room for a constructive ARPU outlook on the call.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean history: the Q1'26 +11% day was driven by capex/FCF, not ARPU. Q2'26 ARPU -2% fell on a -4.1% day.
findings.why_not_priced: The hikes came in the same week as the SpaceX spectrum sell-off (TSX telecom -4.2% on 2026-10-09). Sector stocks kept falling into mid-October on yields and satellite fears, so the price-discipline signal was drowned out. Had it been priced, Canadian telcos would have outperformed after the hikes rather than hitting multi-year lows.
findings.independence: Desjardins upgrade citing quiet back-to-school promos: https://www.cantechletter.com/2026/09/this-analyst-just-upgraded-rogers-communications-to-buy/ (403, snippet only). Management comment on less discounting: Quartr CIBC summary (shared with the net-adds finding). This is a proxy for Q4 ARPU; it is Q4, not the reported quarter.

findings.finding: The CRTC ban on activation and modification fees took effect 2026-06-12, so Q3 is the first full quarter without them. Q2 mobile phone ARPU was already -2% (C$54.25 vs 55.45). The CRTC has also opened a show-cause proceeding on Rogers' replacement C$40 device-setup and C$25 shipping charges, with penalties of up to C$10M.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2'26 ARPU -2% came with a -4.1% day (mixed causes).
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: management flagged it on the Q2 call ('I don't anticipate a substantial change in that in the coming quarters'). What remains open is whether the replacement fees survive the CRTC, a risk to the offset. If the market believed the offset was at risk, consensus revenue would sit lower; it is at +1% YoY.

findings.finding: Guidance arithmetic from the company's own numbers. H1'26 adj EBITDA was C$4,806M, +4%, above the FY +1-3% range, and H1 FCF was C$1,758M (+16%). The CFO said H2 capex will run about C$550M a quarter, against C$964M in Q3'25, so Q3 FCF should rise sharply from C$829M. FY FCF tracks the middle to upper half of C$4.1-4.3B, which leaves room to narrow EBITDA/FCF toward the top.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The FCF guide raise and capex cut in Q1'26 sent the shares up >11% intraday (rbr.com 2026-04-22). A reaffirmed guide in Q2'26 came with -4.1%.
findings.why_not_priced: The capex cut is in the guide, so a big Q3 FCF number lands inside what was guided. The open question is whether the range moves, and nothing says it will. FY service revenue at +3-5% implies flat to negative H2 against H1's +9%, as MLSE is lapped and Q4'25 had the Blue Jays' World Series run, so a raise is far from certain. Size kept small.
findings.independence: Capex run-rate quote from the Q2 call: https://www.webull.com/news/15273923787236352 . Q3'25 capex/FCF: https://finviz.com/news/201756/rogers-communications-reports-third-quarter-2025-results .

findings.finding: Cost program flowing into H2 opex. In late April 2026 Rogers offered voluntary departure and retirement packages to about 10,000 of its roughly 25,000 employees. In July it cut 230 sports and media jobs and an undisclosed number of front-line customer-service agents. Q2 wireless margin was already +70bp, and Q3 is the first full quarter after departures.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior quarter isolated this line.
findings.why_not_priced: Uptake and savings have never been disclosed (Desjardins: 'details on the attractiveness of the packages are unknown'), so consensus cannot model them precisely. That said, the EPS estimate has not moved, which suggests analysts are not pricing a large saving.
findings.independence: July cuts: https://www.iphoneincanada.ca/2026/07/17/rogers-cuts-customer-service-jobs-media-layoffs/ . This overlaps the EPS-bar finding (same EBITDA line), so it is sized small to avoid double counting.

findings.finding: The Blue Jays finished 79-83 and were eliminated on 2026-09-23. Q3 home attendance was strong (snippet: 3.33M, about 41,220 a game), but there will be no Q4 postseason against Q4'25's World Series run. Management will have to frame a weak Q4 media comparison inside the FY guide.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely public: the elimination is widely known and the FY guide (set in January, reaffirmed in July) presumably did not assume a repeat World Series. Kept small because the residual risk is in how Q4 is framed.

findings.finding: Sports monetization update possible on the call. The C$4.35B Kilmer 25% MLSE buyout is due to close in Q4 pending league approvals. The minority sale of the combined sports entity (Rogers says worth more than C$25B) is targeted for H1 2027. Sportico's September 2026 ranking puts the Maple Leafs at US$4.8B, +13% YoY, and Desjardins upgraded on sports valuations and 'upcoming private market valuation updates'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The July 2026 Kilmer announcement and Q2 MLSE put-liability charge came with -4.1% on print day. There is no history of a monetization update moving the stock up.
findings.why_not_priced: The minority-sale value is the main sum-of-the-parts lever and remains unquantified. Rogers trades near a 52-week low, suggesting the market gives little credit. Closing approvals or an early read on the sale could be disclosed on the 10-23 call, but nothing indicates one will be.

findings.finding: Depressed sector positioning into the print. Rogers is -13% YTD and the TSX telecom index -16% against the TSX +11%. Drivers are bond yields, SpaceX/Starlink fears after the 2026-10-09 US spectrum deal, and price competition. NYSE short interest fell from 18.1M (Aug 31) to 14.2M (Sep 30). TD's Valentini and Newhaven call the fears overblown, and Rogers is the only big-three carrier with a live satellite service.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1'26, coming off low expectations, rose >11% intraday on a guide change.
findings.why_not_priced: This is the price itself: low expectations make an in-line print with reassuring commentary on satellite and pricing more likely to lift the stock than to sink it. But the sector drivers (yields, BoC hike odds for 10-28) are macro and outside Rogers' control.
findings.independence: Short-interest series: https://equibles.com/stocks/rci/shortinterest . Satellite as complement, from the Quartr CIBC summary (shared with the net-adds finding).

outside_window.finding: Bank of Canada decision on 2026-10-28, with markets pricing about a 25% chance of a hike. Rates and yields are a named driver of the telecom sell-off.
Kilmer/MLSE 25% buyout closing (Q4, league approvals) and the minority-stake sale (target H1 2027) to fund deleveraging. S&P has Rogers' BBB- on negative outlook.
Peer Q3 prints from BCE, Telus and Quebecor come in early November, after Rogers, so they cannot inform this print.

Uptake or savings from the voluntary departure program: never disclosed

baseline_tension: There is no usable skew. What I found leans mildly positive against a tape near 52-week lows with sector-wide pessimism, so it does not fight a market statement, but the evidence is mostly inference and pulls both ways. p_up stays near 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (fact is not reaction): EPS-bar finding cut from +0.7 to +0.4, because this name moved +11% on an EPS miss and -4.1% on a beat; p_up from 54 to 53.
Lesson 6 (bar): EPS bar disputed across Yahoo (C$1.24), Chartmill (C$1.28) and MarketBeat (~C$1.18); EPS findings kept capped small and the bar dispute stated.

Lesson 3 (caveat reaches number): guidance-arithmetic finding cut from +0.6 to +0.4 for the H2 service-revenue and Q4 World Series comp caveat; pricing finding from +0.6 to +0.5 because it is a Q4 proxy.
Lesson 5 (proxy vs company number): net-adds finding cut from -1.0 to -0.8, since the trend is public and the jobs data is only a proxy; it rests on company Q2 and Q3'25 numbers.
Lessons 'reaction history from wrong events' / 8: rebuilt the scale from confirmed prints (+11%, -4.1%, +5%) and raised abs_move_pct from 4.0 to 5.0.
Cost-savings finding from +0.3 to +0.2 (overlaps the EPS line); Blue Jays from -0.3 to -0.2 (public).
